title: Mobile Crane Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.180)
subtitle: For frequent, periodic, idle-crane and standby-crane inspections, monthly rope checks and lift set-up.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
For any defect, have it carefully examined and decide whether it is a safety hazard, as 1910.180(d)(3) and (d)(4) require; record what was found and done.
The manufacturer's instructions and your site rules may add checks to this list.

sections.title: Operator, Records and Readiness
items: The person at the controls has been designated by the employer to operate this crane.
Durable chart with legible letters and figures fixed in the cab, readable from the seated control position.
Record for brakes, hooks and ropes made this month, signed and dated, with the crane's serial number or other ID, and readily at hand.
Thorough rope inspection done within the past month; record on file with date, inspector signature and rope identifier.
A crane idle one month or more but under 6 months was inspected under (d)(3) and (g)(2)(ii) before returning to service.
A crane idle for six months had a complete inspection covering (d)(3), (d)(4) and (g)(2)(ii) before returning to service.
Standby crane given the (d)(3) and (g)(2)(ii) inspection at least semiannually.
Rope that sat idle for a month or more was thoroughly inspected and approved before use, with a signed, dated record.
Full ballast or counterweight specified by the maker in place and not exceeded; a truck crane that has dropped it is used only temporarily, with special care, for light loads.
Carbon dioxide, dry chemical or equivalent extinguisher in the cab or near the crane.

sections.title: Frequent Inspection Items (Also Part of the Periodic Inspection)
items: Controls operate properly with no maladjustment; checked daily.
No excessive component wear; no lubricant or foreign matter fouling control mechanisms.
Every safety device functions with no malfunction.
No leakage or deterioration in the air or hydraulic systems; checked daily.
No cracks or deformation; throat opening no more than 15 percent over normal; twist no more than 10° from the plane of the unbent hook.
Works properly; no signs of excessive deterioration and no dirt or moisture build-up.

sections.title: Periodic Inspection Items
items: No deformed, cracked or corroded members anywhere in the structure or boom.
No cracked or worn sheaves or drums.
Pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices free of wear, cracks and distortion.
No excessive wear on brake and clutch parts, linings, pawls or ratchets.
Load, boom angle and other indicators read accurately across their full range.
Gasoline, diesel, electric or other power plant performs properly and meets safety requirements.
No excessive sprocket wear or chain stretch.
Travel steering, braking and locking devices work without malfunction.
No excessively worn or damaged tires.

sections.title: Wire Rope
items: No reduction below nominal diameter from loss of core support, corrosion or outside-wire wear.
Any broken outside wires counted and their concentration judged not to be a hazard.
No corroded or broken wires at end connections.
End connections not corroded, cracked, bent or worn, and correctly applied.
No severe kinking, crushing, cutting or unstranding.
Rope at equalizer sheaves, limited-travel sheaves and saddles checked closely for heavy wear and broken wires.
Nonrotating rope given a close, careful inspection.
Hoist rope free of kinks before hoisting starts.
Part lines not twisted around each other.

sections.title: Set-Up and Lifting
items: Load, including blocks, hooks and slings, does not exceed the chart rating for the radius.
Crane is level and blocked where necessary.
Load well secured and balanced in the sling or lifting device before it goes higher than a few inches.
Outriggers set whenever the load at the planned radius exceeds the manufacturer's no-outrigger rating.
Any floats in use are securely attached to the outriggers.
Wood blocks strong enough to prevent crushing.
Wood blocks wide and long enough that they cannot shift or topple under load.
Hook brought over the load so the load will not swing.
No one rides the hook or the load during any hoisting, lowering, swinging or travel.

references: 29 CFR 1910.180: Crawler locomotive and truck cranes (OSHA, Part 1910 Subpart N: Materials Handling and Storage)
